Commentary.Commentary: Tim Southee received the Man of the Match award for his outstanding bowling. That brings an end to Pakistan's tour of New Zealand. Now they will head to Australia for a 3-match Test and 5-match ODI series. But before that New Zealand will be visiting their Trans-Tasman rivals for a 3-match ODI series. We will look forward to your company then. Cheers!

The opening partnership meant that Pakistan had got to a position of safety from where they could harbor slight hopes of having a slight crack at the total. The visitors needed 211 runs from a minimum of 34 overs in the final session. It was always going to be a mammoth task despite having nine wickets in the bank but the visitors thought they could try, thinking perhaps they couldn't lose. Can't blame them, can you? Only Pakistan could have done such suicidal damage. The Kiwis deservedly sweep the series with a commanding 2-0 win.

Armed with a handy 55-run lead, New Zealand rode on a blistering Taylor century to up the ante with a notable innings from Latham. The others chipped in too as the hosts declared very late on day four, setting Pakistan an improbable target of 369. Having seen off the tricky 3-over phase to stumps on day 4, openers Azhar and Aslam stitched a very gritty opening stand that had batted out more than half of the overs on day five.

The Test had started well for Pakistan after opting to bowl in favourable conditions. They had NZ at 119/5 but the lower order dug in to get the score to a competitive 271. Sohail Khan and Imran Khan were the star performers with the ball while Amir was unlucky not to get more wickets due to dropped catches. In reply, Pakistan's top half was blown away to leave them reeling at 51/5 at one stage. Babar Azam's unbeaten 90 and his partnerships with Sarfraz and Sohail helped restore some pride for the visitors.

DAY 5 - Unimaginable scenes! Pakistan have imploded in a manner only they possibly can. The score read 158/1 at tea with a draw looking more than imminent. The dismissals of Babar and Aslam just after the break set the tone and it was a procession from there on. Not sure what the visiting batsmen gulped at the break but they fell like nine pins in the final session, losing nine wickets for just 72 runs. Incredible! This is New Zealand's first ever series win over Pakistan in 31 years.

So we are down to the final day of the series. Pakistan will have to face a minimum of 98 overs tomorrow to try and save this Test. Doubt whether they will go to try and chase down 369 to level the series. Their unbeaten record in Test series in New Zealand since 1985, in all likelihood, is about to be broken. Join us at 0300 IST (2130 GMT, previous day) tomorrow for all the action from Day 5. Adios! Take Care!

Pakistan will not be too disappointed. The water had already gone above head level and they were just aiming to delay New Zealand's declaration, which they achieved. It was a toil for them and Imran Khan managed to pick up three wickets.

STUMPS ON DAY 4! A pretty meaningless declaration from New Zealand, considering that there was not much time left in the day to take wickets. The Kiwis batted well today, riding on Ross Taylor's century and a magnificent 80 from Latham. Williamson waited for Taylor's century before calling his men in, probably hoping for an early wicket.
